correctness.rationale: Every finite-energy canonical form has a Laurent expansion. Fiber Parseval makes each coefficient locally L² at the puncture; removable singularities and modulus-periodicity make it entire and bounded, hence constant. Character equivariance leaves precisely the annihilator qZ. Their orthogonal norms C_k are exact, yielding the diagonal evaluation kernel. A positive geometric-series bound gives the sharp large-order expansion uniformly on compact subannuli. The torsion set in the real character torus is countable dense, and bounded orders comprise finite sets, proving continuity exactly off torsion and upper semicontinuity. A strict plurisubharmonic exhaustion ensures Steinness; standalone finite checks corroborate but are not the proof.

value.rationale: It is a natural complete analysis of the holonomy parameter ignored by a newly important one-dimensional Bergman construction. It exhibits dense jumps of infinite algebraic dimension across a smooth Stein family, while quantifying that the evaluation-density jump shrinks sharply at rate q[(t/2)^(2q)+t^(-2q)] on compact interiors. This resolves a concrete boundary between algebraic dimension instability and analytic kernel stability rather than a contrived subcase.
